utterances.text: After being released from the armed forces, what did you do in terms of work or occupation?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: I had work obligation in a company set up during the war. It was called Energoinvest Automatika.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And two questions from that. First of all, what is meant by the term "work obligation"?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Well, it's a part of practically civilian engagement for war effort, so it's similar to military obligatory service, only we were obliged to work in different areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And then the second question is: Energoinvest Automatika, was that something different from Energoinvest, where you had been working before you were in the armed forces?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: What kind of a company was Energoinvest Automatika? What did they make?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Energoinvest Automatika was made up of several former Energoinvest companies operating in Stup, in Ilidza.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And when you say "several former Energoinvest companies," what sort of product did these companies make and -- that became Energoinvest Automatika, what business were they in?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Generally speaking, it was not a standard manufacture, so to speak. One of the main tasks of this company, since this location of Energoinvest was practically on the front line, was to preserve as much equipment of the former units of the factory that existed at that location. So we managed to produce something but mainly by using the existing equipment to manufacture finished products out the semi-finished products.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Now moving ahead, did you ever have occasion to go to the Pretis factory in Vogosca in the north of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Can you tell Their Honours the circumstances under which you first went to the Pretis factory and why you went there.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Sometime in spring, I should say, 1995, it was hinted to me that I should go to Pretis and seek advice from some people there regarding the modification, as we were told at the time, of electrical components used for the so-called aerial bomb launcher.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And did you in fact go to the Pretis factory?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: How long after you got what you call hints was it that you went to the Pretis factory? I'm sorry, did -- let me ask the question again. You say that it was hinted to you that you should go to Pretis. And then my question is: How long after the hints was it that you actually did go to Pretis?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly. About ten days, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And when you went to the Pretis factory the first time, did you go alone or did you go with anyone else?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: A colleague of mine, Desimir Popovic, from Automatika was with me, and we were also accompanied by Mr. Mitrovic [realtime transcript read in error "Mijatovic"] from -- from the brigade --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the name of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Could you repeat the name of the brigade, please? It didn't come through, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: I'm sorry, it says here Mitrovic, whereas I said Mijatovic, and it was the Ilidza Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: When you went to the Pretis factory, did you meet anyone there?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Who did you meet?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: We met Mr. Krsmanovic. I think he was a major.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And did Mr. Krsmanovic tell you anything about what he did at the Pretis factory?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: He didn't tell us what he was doing at Pretis, but we were taken to him as a person who would be a liaison person with regard to the job that we were supposed to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And what was the job that you were supposed to do?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: This job involved modification for a -- launching air bombs from the launcher.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Who was it that explained this to you? Was it Major Krsmanovic, Mr. Mijatovic, someone else?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Mr. Mijatovic was not present at this meeting. We talked with Mr. Krsmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: What was it -- why did the -- why did the launcher have to be modified? What was the driving force behind making a modification?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR SOJA
utterances.text: Mr. Krsmanovic was against modification. He thought nothing should be modified and that bringing in electrical and electronic components will render the whole equipment unreliable. However, the Ilidza Brigade and our company requested us that we nonetheless perform this modification.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And my question is: If you're being requested to perform a modification, presumably it is because there is some problem or other. Did anyone tell you there was a problem with the way the air bombs were being launched up until then; and if the answer to that is yes, can you tell Their Honours who said it and what they said?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Isailovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. It seems like Mr. Docherty is putting answers in the witness's mouth. I think that the witness did not really talk about the problem that he is -- problems that Mr. Docherty is mentioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, I can't agree with you. His question is if you're going requested to make a modification, then what was the problem that gave rise to this request? That's -- why the modification? Why was the modification necessary? That's the -- or what occasioned the modification. I don't see anything that is improper in that. But I think we will have to wait for that answer tomorrow, Mr. Docherty, because we're now at 7.00. We adjourn until 2.15 tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 25th day of April, 2007, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.01 p.m.,
